page: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-16GB is a virtualized server based on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, providing 6 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with single-thread-per-core topology. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2.67 GB per vCPU core. Hardware acceleration is not present, with 0 GPUs provisioned. Local storage is omitted entirely, requiring reliance on external storage volumes for disk operations. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates notable variance between burst and sustained execution. Geekbench metrics show strong performance in single-core compute with a score of 2028.0 and text processing at 2628.0, alongside mid-range multi-core performance at 8549.0 and clang compilation at 10563.0. In contrast, heavy continuous execution via stress-ng places both single-core (787.9) and multi-core (4703.94) results in the lower percentiles. Memory subsystem throughput reflects standard read bandwidth of 43.56 GB/sec for large blocks, but uncached write bandwidth settles at a weaker 24.88 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reaches 5.86 GB/sec, while in-memory operations remain stable with Redis achieving 8.81 million operations per second.

Because it relies on shared CPU cores and dispenses with bundled local storage, the instance exhibits high resource density and cost efficiency for non-constant compute profiles. Tradeoffs include lack of AVX-512 vector extensions, lower sustained compute stability under full utilization, and reliance on remote storage. The platform fits containerized microservices, dev and test environments, CI/CD build agents, and distributed task queues that benefit from multi-vCPU concurrency without requiring continuous dedicated hardware allocation.
